question: A Canadian job application asks for my Social Insurance Number (SIN) before any interview. Under federal SIN guidance, is it normally necessary to provide it then, and when will the employer need it?
generated_answer: The SIN is a nine-digit number that you will need to work in Canada and to access government programs and benefits. You must provide your SIN to your employer within 3 days of starting your job. If you do not have a SIN, you must apply for one. You can apply for a SIN at a Service Canada Centre. You will need to provide proof of your identity and your immigration status. You can also apply for a SIN online. You will need to provide the same information as you would if you were applying in person. Once you have applied for a SIN, you will receive a letter with your SIN number. You should keep this letter safe, as you will need to provide it to your employer when you start your job. If you do not have a SIN, you may be able to work in Canada without one, but you will not be able to access government programs and benefits. You will also be required to pay taxes on your income, even if you do not have a SIN. It is important to note that you should never provide your SIN to anyone who is not authorized to have it. This includes your employer, unless they are required to have it for tax purposes. If you are unsure about whether you need to provide your SIN, you should contact Service Canada for more information.
